question: On deterministic finite linear-network fixtures, does the restriction-aware spectral operator preserve the same local compatibility residual information as an independently computed local-residual baseline, reduce exactly to the scalar graph Laplacian when restrictions are rank-one identities, and remain invariant under representational changes that should not alter the mathematics?
hypothesis: sheaf.real.spectral_v1 agrees exactly with sheaf.real.local_residual_v1 on compatibility energy, collapses to graph.scalar_laplacian_v1 under scalar identity restrictions, preserves residuals under known kernel translations, and preserves Laplacian/spectrum under edge-orientation reversal

datasets.grid: declared vertices and edges; no geographic interpretation
datasets.quality_control_policy: fixture dimensions, finiteness, restriction shapes, expected energies, and expected nullities are executable test conditions

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: all synthetic cases comparing assembled-coboundary energy to independently computed edge-local restriction residual energy
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: any missing case or unavailable comparison is experiment failure
primary_metrics.uncertainty_method: deterministic FP64 equality within a declared numerical tolerance

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: rank-one identity-restriction fixtures compared with the ordinary scalar graph Laplacian
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: absence of the identity-restriction collapse witness is experiment failure
primary_metrics.uncertainty_method: deterministic FP64 equality within a declared numerical tolerance

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: each fixture before and after reversing every edge orientation while swapping endpoint restriction maps
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: any fixture without its orientation metamorphic witness is experiment failure
primary_metrics.uncertainty_method: deterministic FP64 equality within a declared numerical tolerance

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: declared fixture perturbations known analytically to lie in ker(D)
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: missing or malformed kernel perturbation witness is experiment failure
primary_metrics.uncertainty_method: deterministic FP64 equality within a declared numerical tolerance

secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: nullity must be reported for every structurally valid fixture

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: each fixture with nonzero coboundary rank
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: absence is allowed only when the coboundary has zero numerical rank

negative_controls: the restriction-aware candidate must not beat the strong local-residual baseline by withholding restriction maps from that baseline; both receive identical endpoint maps
rank-one identity restrictions must collapse to the ordinary graph incidence/Laplacian construction rather than produce a distinct sheaf-only result
reversing edge orientation and swapping endpoint restriction maps must not change L0 or singular values
adding a vector known from the declared restriction map to lie in ker(D) must not change the compatibility residual
malformed dimensions and non-finite section/restriction values must fail closed rather than produce plausible diagnostics
falsifiers: assembled-coboundary compatibility energy disagrees with the independently computed local-residual energy outside the declared FP64 tolerance
the identity-restriction special case differs from the ordinary graph Laplacian outside tolerance
edge-orientation reversal changes L0, nullity, or singular values outside tolerance
a declared kernel translation changes the compatibility residual outside tolerance
the candidate is credited with incremental scientific detection value on the basis of this structural experiment alone
split_policy: not applicable; deterministic structural fixtures with additional hidden regression fixtures allowed only for implementation hardening
preprocessing: none; matrices and sections are consumed exactly as declared in the fixture
stopping_rule: the structural experiment passes only if every primary invariant holds for every required fixture; any later fault-localization or climate-data experiment must be separately preregistered and cannot inherit success from this experiment
multiple_comparison_policy: not applicable to deterministic algebraic/metamorphic invariants; any later parameter sweep must report all attempted variants
